audit.whatIsWrong: Stages 4-5, Level 6 and First item were scored Lucian/Skill/Skill while the whys for those same rows say the tank dictates trades, that Level 6 is 'his single biggest window', and that his first tank item makes him near-immune.
audit.why: 43.14% over 51 games, and the packet chart gives Nautilus stages 4 through 7. Riptide (7/6.5/6/5.5/5s) blunts the kite from level 4, and Dredge Line into Depth Charge is a lockdown chain from 6.
audit.corrected: phases[3..5].side and win[3..5] -> Nautilus, proposed as matched pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4]/[5] described Lucian's own spikes and ignored the enemy's, even though the content layer already identifies Level 6 and his first tank item as Nautilus spikes.
audit.why: Depth Charge (120/100/80s) chained off Dredge Line is the matchup's decisive spike; the first tank item is the second.
audit.corrected: Level 6 = hook into Depth Charge, never channel The Culling with the hook up; First item = his burst immunity.

audit.whatIsWrong: Titan's Wrath was never mentioned anywhere in either layer, and Staggering Blow's root was described only vaguely.
audit.why: Titan's Wrath is a 12s flat-cooldown shield that eats exactly the burst window Lucian is trying to open, and Staggering Blow roots on his first attack against a target — that is what removes the dash exit after a hook lands.
audit.corrected: Force the shield out before committing; treat first contact as the root, not the hook alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere (sequencingCues 0). Every line said 'track the hook' with no number.
audit.why: Dredge Line is 14/13/12/11/10s at 1150 range — long enough that counting it gives a real step-up window. Riptide at 5-7s does not.
audit.corrected: Dredge Line's 14s rank-1 cooldown written into dosFull[0], Riptide's cycle into phases[3].

audit.whatIsWrong: early, mid and late were written in the first person ('the only phase I genuinely own', 'this is where I lose'), breaking the second-person voice used everywhere else on the page.
audit.why: The rest of the file addresses the reader directly; a first-person block reads as a different author and undercuts the advice.
audit.corrected: All three rewritten in second person, same facts, within the length band.

audit.why: The packet's suspectName 'Hold Relentless Pursuit' is a false positive — Relentless Pursuit is Lucian's real E name.

edits.before: Keep the pressure rolling but track Dredge Line (Hook) — your lead is HP-bar bullying, not all-in math, until items arrive.
edits.after: Riptide is up every 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s and the slow blunts your kite, so his 1150-range hook now dictates where you stand.

edits.before: The Culling adds lane-clear and execute chip — use it through walls on recalls and low-HP escapes.
edits.after: Dredge Line into Depth Charge is a full lockdown chain — never channel The Culling with his hook up.

edits.before: First item spike is your kill window — the dash-weave combo now deletes half bars. Force the issue before he stabilizes.
edits.after: His first tank item eats your burst while one hook still chains you into Depth Charge — trade only when Q is down.

edits.before: His only real engage — dodge it and the lane is free. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: Dredge Line is 14s at rank 1 — count it down, and step up only inside that window.

edits.before: Nautilus spends Dredge Line (Hook) early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Titan's Wrath (12s) shields his burst window — force the shield out before you commit.

edits.before: That’s Nautilus’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: His passive roots on first contact — one hook and the whole chain lands on you.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are the only phase I genuinely own, and even then it's a knife-edge. My long auto range plus the Lightslinger double-tap off Piercing Light lets me chip him every time he steps to last-hit, and at 2 I can land a brutal double-shot trade before he has Riptide and Depth Charge online. The one rule: never stand still in his Dredge Line range. If he lands the hook, his passive root locks me in place and a squishy Lucian eats the entire CC chain. I dash with Relentless Pursuit to break spacing, not to chase.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are the only phase you genuinely own, and even then it's a knife-edge. Your long auto range plus the Lightslinger double-tap off Piercing Light chips him every time he steps to last-hit, and at 2 you land a real double-shot trade before Riptide and Depth Charge are online. The one rule: never stand still inside Dredge Line's 1150 range. If the hook lands, his passive roots you on contact and a squishy Lucian eats the whole CC chain. Dash with Relentless Pursuit to break spacing, not to chase.

edits.before: From 4-5 the lane starts slipping. His Riptide slow makes it far harder for me to kite, and Ardent Blaze move speed only helps if I haven't already been hooked. At 6 it's his window outright: Dredge Line into Depth Charge knockup is a guaranteed full-duration lockdown, and my low base HP gets bursted by him plus the jungler before The Culling can do anything. I don't channel R into a Nautilus who has his hook up — one Q pull and I'm dead mid-channel. Bait the hook, dash it, and only trade when it's down.
edits.after: From 4-5 the lane slips. Riptide is back every 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s and its slow makes kiting far harder, and Ardent Blaze move speed only helps if you haven't already been hooked. At 6 it's his window outright: Dredge Line into Depth Charge is a guaranteed lockdown chain, and your low base HP gets burst by him plus the jungler before The Culling matters. Never channel R against a Nautilus holding his hook — one pull and you die mid-channel. Bait the hook, dash it, and trade only while it's down.

edits.before: This is where I lose, plainly. I'm a weak scaler for an ADC top, and a full-tank Nautilus shrugs off my physical burst while a single Dredge Line drags me out of position into a knockup my team can't peel. His passive auto-root kills my entire kiting identity — the thing that beats slow tanks doesn't work on one who roots me on contact. So I have to close this lane on my level 2-3 double-shot windows and snowball that lead elsewhere; if it goes even into items, he wins. Late game my job is to never get caught alone, group, and fire The Culling only after his hook and R are spent.
